exercise.name: Resistance Band Standing Y-Raise

reference.title: Resistance Band Standing Y-Raise
reference.listing: Video (movement reference only; the page could not be fetched from the authoring environment (the proxy refused gymvisual.com), so the movement follows the name and standard coaching)

exercise.bodyPart: Shoulders and upper back (deltoids, lower and middle trapezius)
exercise.mechanics: Isolation (shoulder elevation with upward rotation of the shoulder blade)

breathing.pattern: Breathe out as you raise, breathe in as you lower.
breathing.cadence: About 2 s up, short pause, about 2 s down

prescription.effort: Stop 2-3 reps short of failure (RIR 2-3); form first
prescription.load: Band tension is user-chosen; light; the band is hardest overhead, where it is stretched most
prescription.progression: More reps or a slower lowering, then a stronger band

cues.text: Stand on the middle of the band, feet hip width, knees soft; hold an end in each hand by the front of the thighs, thumbs up.
Breathe out and raise the straight arms up and out into a Y, thumbs leading.
Arms overhead in a Y, thumbs pointing back; ribs down, shoulders away from the ears.
Lower slowly in about 2 s against the band.
Brief pause by the thighs, then repeat.

mistakes.mistake: Arching the low back to get the arms higher
mistakes.fix: Ribs down, glutes and abs braced; raise only as high as the back stays still.

mistakes.mistake: Shrugging the shoulders up to the ears
mistakes.fix: Let the shoulder blades turn up but keep the neck long; use a lighter band.

mistakes.mistake: Arms drifting in front of the face (a front raise)
mistakes.fix: Keep the arms out in a Y, a little in front of the body.

mistakes.mistake: Letting the band snap the arms down

kinematics.norm: Arms overhead to about 135-145 degrees (a Y, about 45 degrees out from vertical), in line with the lower trapezius fibres; an overhead raise in that line gave the highest lower trapezius activity among the exercises tested (Ekstrom 2003, prone)
A Y: about 30-45 degrees in front of the frontal plane (scapular plane, Tsuruike 2019)
Arms long, elbows soft and steady (clinical opinion)

Elastic tension rises as the band stretches, so the load is highest where the band is longest; at matched effort, elastic tubing and dumbbells gave similar muscle activity in upper-body exercises (Andersen 2010); with the band under the feet the load is highest overhead
Slow, about 2 s up and 2 s down (clinical opinion)

sources.title: GymVisual #24717, Resistance Band Standing Y-Raise, video (movement reference)
Ekstrom, Donatelli & Soderberg 2003, surface electromyographic analysis of exercises for the trapezius and serratus anterior muscles (J Orthop Sports Phys Ther 33(5):247-258)
Tsuruike & Ellenbecker 2019, scapular muscle electromyographic activity during abduction exercises in the scapular plane in three positions (Int J Sports Phys Ther 14(6):935-944)

Andersen, Andersen, Mortensen, Poulsen, Bjornlund and Zebis 2010, muscle activation and perceived loading during rehabilitation exercises: comparison of dumbbells and elastic resistance (Phys Ther 90(4):538-549)

cautions: Stop if sharp pain, a pinching feeling at the top of the shoulder, numbness or tingling occurs.
Band tension is user-chosen: pick a light band you can control overhead.

Check the band for nicks or tears before each set and make sure it cannot slip off its anchor (under the feet, round the upright). Stand firmly on its middle so it cannot slip out from under the feet.
Muscle glow colours and activation curves are illustrative, not measured EMG.
modify: Shoulder pinch overhead: stop at about 120 degrees, or step off the band and do it with no load.
Too hard at the top: step on the band with one foot only.
progressions: Band incline Y raise (chest on an incline bench).

muscleNotes.serratus_l: Turns the shoulder blade up so the arm can go overhead.

muscleNotes.upper_traps_l: Turns the shoulder blade up with the serratus; shrugging overloads it.

muscleNotes.post_deltoid_l: Helps hold the arm in the Y.
